evidence.curator_note: Book draws 0 arc(s) on the intact steroid: the reaction arrow carries only the label 'alpha' and the starting structure bears no '+' and no '.' at all. Both encoded moves are therefore implicit, and the regiochemistry is read off the DRAWN PRODUCT, which prints '+' on C13 and '.' on C17 -- i.e. the C13-C17 bond of ring D is the ionized sigma bond. Move <1> sends one of its two electrons to 'external' (the EI ionization hole; same convention as the saturated-hydrocarbon M+. records IMS4-EQ4.3a / IMS4-EQ4.7 / IMS4-EQ4.8, where the precursor SMILES is the neutral closed-shell hydrocarbon and charge=1/radical_electrons=1 live in the species fields), move <2> is the implicit homolysis hook that puts the odd electron on C17. Neither is drawn on the page.

locator.section: 9.1 Hydrocarbons (rH labelled on the second reaction arrow)

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 1 arc: one curved arrow that starts on the C18-H bond (the angular methyl is spelled out as 'H2C-H' to single out the migrating hydrogen), arches over the top of the structure and points down at the C17 radical site. Move <1> encodes exactly that arc, compressed into the net C17 -> C18 radical migration of the H-ATOM transfer; the hydrogen itself is implicit in the mapped SMILES (same compression as the canonical rH record IMS4-EQ4.33). The remaining hooks of a fully resolved H-atom transfer (the C17 odd electron reaching the H, and the second C18-H electron staying on C18) are NOT drawn on the page.

locator.section: 9.1 Hydrocarbons (rH labelled on the third reaction arrow)

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arc(s) on this structure: (i) a short fishhook leaving the C18 radical (printed 'H2C.') and pointing down-left at the hydrogen that is written out explicitly on C16, and (ii) a long fishhook from that C16-H bond back up to C18. Move <1> encodes both arcs as the net C18 -> C16 radical migration of the H-atom transfer, the hydrogen being implicit in the mapped SMILES. The third hook of a fully resolved H-atom transfer (the second C16-H electron remaining on C16) is not drawn on the page.

locator.section: 9.1 Hydrocarbons (alpha labelled on the fourth reaction arrow)

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn (a fishhook from the C16 radical into the forming C15=C16 pi bond, and a fishhook from the C14-C15 sigma bond into the same forming pi bond), and move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page) -- it carries the second C14-C15 electron to C14, which is where the drawn m/z 218 product prints its '.' next to the '+' on C13. The expelled neutral is drawn as CH2=CHCH2R.

GENERIC SCHEME, CURATOR-INSTANTIATED. Eq 9.8 is drawn with 'R' on C17 and with wavy bonds standing in for rings A/B in the second and later structures; the only number printed anywhere in the scheme is 'm/z 218' under the final ion. The instantiation used here is 5-alpha-pregnane (C21H36, M+. m/z 288, i.e. R = the C20-C21 ethyl side chain), which is forced by the printed numbers: those 288 M+. and 273 labels are NOT on this record's page -- they belong to Figure 9.3 on printed p234 (PDF 245), captioned 'Mass spectrum of 5-alpha-pregnane', whose inset structure draws the C17 ethyl (verified at native resolution); the first draft implied they sat on p235, and 288 - C5H10 (the drawn CH2=CHCH2R with R = C2H5, 70 u) = 218, while eq 9.9 on the same page draws the C17 side chain explicitly as an ethyl group. All m/z values in this record are monoisotopic values computed for that instantiation; the page prints no intensities. Stereochemistry (5-alpha / trans A-B ring fusion, drawn with a dashed H at C5 in eq 9.9) is deliberately NOT encoded in the mapped SMILES. Atom map numbers are the standard steroid carbon numbers C1-C21.

NO MØD RULE CROSS-LINK. data/mechanisms/rule_index.json 'by_equation' covers only chapters 4 and 8 (57 equations) and has no entry for 9.8, so no rule variable can be cited. The nearest generic candidates in the rule set were inspected and REJECTED: 'sigma_lowIE' ([_A+.]1[I]2>>[_A.]1.[I+]2) needs an iodine/low-IE heteroatom partner and cannot describe a C-C sigma ionization; 'hTransition_saturated_1/2/3/4' all require an H...C-C-C-C-[_A+.] (or [_A+]) receptor chain of a fixed length terminating on the charge/radical site, whereas the two rH steps here move a hydrogen between C18 and C17 (and back between C16 and C18) across a ring-opened chain of six atoms whose charge site (C13+) sits in the middle rather than at the receptor terminus; 'hTransition_saturated_2_alpha' ([C.]1[C]2([_A+]3)[C]4[C]5>>[C]1{=}[C]2[C]4[C]5.[_A+.]3) has the right radical-site alpha topology but cleaves the bond to the CHARGE-BEARING atom, so the charge departs with the neutral, while in eq 9.8 the cleaved C14-C15 bond is two bonds from C13+ (the first draft said 'remote', which overstates the separation) and the charge is retained by the ion. Chapter 9 steroid hydrocarbon chemistry is simply not represented in the current rule set.
